clue.text: Amphibian, looking angry unfortunately, about to devour fellow

indicators.note: something that devours another takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other
about here means turned round, so the joined words are read from the other end

parts.note: to see red is to look angry; red-faced with rage
alas is an exclamation of misfortune
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A creature looks angry, sadly, just before it eats a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does not surround anything here: it turns the first two pieces round together, and only then does the fellow go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The salamander is a lizard-like creature of the newt family, a typical amphibian.

clue.text: Cry before party, as one become sombre?

parts.note: to sob is to cry
ere is an old word for before
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone weeps ahead of a celebration, as a person turned gloomy might.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party. 'As one become sombre' is an old-fashioned way of saying like someone who has become serious.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sobered up is to have become serious and grave again, so it describes a person turned solemn.

clue.text: Short excursion into byway to find loo

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter is lopped off
going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a lane is a minor road or byway
a trip is an excursion, with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A walker takes a brief detour down a side road looking for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, especially in a camp or barracks, and loo is the informal British word for toilet.

clue.text: Do you ultimately collaborate in fact?

parts.note: to act is to do

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of you
to ally is to join forces or collaborate

explanation.surface: A question asking whether someone really does cooperate in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually and in fact are interchangeable adverbial phrases meaning really, as a matter of truth.

clue.text: Deprived of religious significance, diehard in sect is put out

indicators.note: put out can mean disturbed or knocked out of place, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A hardline member of a religious sect is expelled and stripped of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To dechristianise something is to remove its Christian character, leaving it secular and without religious meaning.

clue.text: Critic of big country half ignored by relations

indicators.note: ignoring half of a word means leaving out half its letters

parts.note: Russia, the world's largest country, with its second half dropped
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A commentator on a large nation is snubbed by half of his own family.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin was the leading Victorian art and social critic, author of Modern Painters.

clue.text: Measures introduced by Hampshire

indicators.note: the answer is brought in by the next word, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: letters two to five of the county name

explanation.surface: New regulations brought in by a county council in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Amps are units measuring electric current, so they are measures in the sense of units.

clue.text: At late hour children turned up — to become these?

definitions.text: At late hour children turned up — to become these?

parts.note: taken as written
ten o'clock is a late hour

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants

explanation.surface: Kids who show up at ten at night thereby become part of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: those who have turned up are present. 'Turned up' does double duty, flipping the children and describing arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendees are people who are present at an event, which is what anyone who turns up becomes.

clue.text: Sacrament in Cornish location denied unknown character

indicators.note: a place denied something has it taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a town near Land's End in Cornwall
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A church rite in a Cornish town is refused to some mysterious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the far south-west county of England; removing the letter for an unknown leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is one of the seven sacraments of the Catholic Church, also called confession or reconciliation.

clue.text: "Suddenly ordinary city" — quote recalled

parts.note: the spa city in Somerset

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is taken in the backwards direction

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A remembered quotation describing a city as abruptly mundane.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an anticlimax, a sudden drop from the elevated to the commonplace, so bathetic describes a jarring shift to the ordinary.

clue.text: Religious organisation, small and lustrous

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: A description of a church group that is small yet shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy fabric, so satiny means smooth with a soft sheen, which is lustrous.

clue.text: Transport system making one complain

explanation.surface: A gripe about a train network that drives passengers to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The link is a joke: the trains are so bad they make you protest about them, which is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the railway as a mode of transport and, as a verb, to protest bitterly.

clue.text: Initially acting like a monarch, we hear, can be trying

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of acting

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound of a word is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: a monarch is reigning; the sound is respelt as the end of the answer

explanation.surface: Playing the part of a king is said to be exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like 'tiresome' but is meant in the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge, the start of putting them on trial.

clue.text: Prepare to eat meal cooked without imaginative content?

indicators.note: cooked food is altered from its raw state, so these letters are rearranged
eating something takes it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to dress food is to prepare it
the letters of meal, rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to make something to eat, with a plain dish lacking flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a sleep without dreams has no imaginative content.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamless sleep has no dreams, the nightly products of imagination, so it is empty of imagined material.

clue.text: A time in which you'll find troubled editors being most skilful

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: these words say the next item sits inside what comes before
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters of editors, rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A period when harassed newspaper editors find themselves at their most capable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'being' so that it reads as an adjective phrase matching the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means deft or clever with hands or mind, so its superlative means most skilful.

clue.text: Rise and stagger round bathroom initially

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of bathroom

explanation.surface: Someone gets up and lurches around the bathroom first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' is the definition in the sense of rising up against authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up in revolt against those in power.

clue.text: Line number up on step briefly in city once

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nine is a number
a grade is a step or level, cut short

explanation.surface: Instructions for drawing a line with a number above a stair.
explanation.definitionFit: Leningrad was the Soviet name of St Petersburg from 1924 to 1991, so it is a former city name.

clue.text: Secluded places about to have special events?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
treats are special occasions or outings

explanation.surface: Quiet hideaways that are going to host special occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet, private place one withdraws to for rest or contemplation.

clue.text: Introduction for piano arranged by unknown composer

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of piano
arr. is the abbreviation for arranged, used in music credits
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A piano prelude set by a composer nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Hubert Parry was an English composer, best known for the hymn tune Jerusalem.

clue.text: Like pine needles maybe in a church got up

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England
rose means got up

explanation.surface: Pine needles, perhaps, found in a church after someone stood up.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual botanical word: the parts are simple, and the definition tells you it is a shape term.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerose is a botanical term for leaves that are narrow, stiff and sharp-pointed, as pine needles are.

clue.text: Daughter has one particular account of things that is amusing

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
I is the Roman numeral for one
a version is one person's account of events

explanation.surface: A girl tells her own entertaining take on what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as 'something that is amusing', a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a pastime or entertainment, something that amuses and takes the mind off other things.

clue.text: It's got to fix a note up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it
taken as written
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone insists a musical note must be pinned higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the definition: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in the bar order gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the abbreviation for Italian vermouth, so the full word is Italian; the clue uses the short form as a crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Worker in better physical shape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mechanic who assembles or installs parts
second meaning: comparative of fit, healthier

explanation.surface: A labourer who has got healthier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitter is a tradesman who puts together machinery, and fitter also compares physical condition.

clue.text: Supplicant, little alien — I will have one request initially

parts.note: petit is French for little, a foreign word
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of request

explanation.surface: A small extraterrestrial makes a plea, starting with a single request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little alien' suggests ET, but alien means foreign: the French word for little.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner is someone who formally asks or begs for something, which is what a supplicant does.

clue.text: Believer taking month to cross India

indicators.note: a word that crosses another is laid across it, so it spans and encloses it

parts.note: Jan is the abbreviation for January
India is the radio code word for I

explanation.surface: A devotee spends a month travelling across India.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jain is a follower of Jainism, an ancient Indian religion, so a religious believer.

clue.text: Most modest expense you accommodated

indicators.note: something accommodated is given room inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a cost is an expense
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: The cheapest bill for putting you up was the most modest.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means shy or bashful, so its superlative describes the most modest or retiring person.

clue.text: More irritable, needing support after game

parts.note: snap is a children's card game
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: Someone grows crankier after a match and needs propping up.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means short-tempered, inclined to speak sharply, so snappier is more irritable.

clue.text: Millions consume what vegetarians won't

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of people eat the food that vegetarians refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows 'consume' from the wordplay for its sense: what vegetarians won't eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetarians by definition avoid animal flesh, which is meat.

clue.text: Acquiescent about editor being given new layout

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: resigned means accepting what cannot be changed
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A meek editor puts up with having the page format changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign is to plan again, so something redesigned has been given a fresh arrangement or look.
